title: 24-day and 21-day workers together
statement: A can finish a piece of work in 24 days and B can finish it in 21 days. How many days will they take working together?
explanation:
In one day A does 1/24 and B does 1/21 of the work; together 1/24 + 1/21 = 5/56 of it.
Time = 1 ÷ 5/56 = **11.2 days**  (shortcut: ab/(a + b) = 504/45).

title: Together in 4 days, A alone in 6: B alone?
statement: A and B together can complete a task in 4 days. A alone can complete it in 6 days. In how many days can B alone complete it?
explanation: B's daily work = 1/4 − 1/6 = 1/12, so B alone takes **12 days**.

title: 25 workers in 6 days → 5 workers
statement: 25 workers can build a wall in 6 days. How many days will 5 workers take to build the same wall, working at the same rate?
explanation: Total work = 25 × 6 = 150 worker-days. With 5 workers: 150 / 5 = **30 days**.

title: Fill in 15 h, empty in 20 h
statement: Pipe A fills a tank in 15 hours and pipe B empties the full tank in 20 hours. If both are opened together on an empty tank, how long will it take to fill?
explanation: Net filling per hour = 1/15 − 1/20 = 1/60. Time = 1 ÷ 1/60 = **60 hours**.

title: A (10 d) and B (12 d) together for 3 days, then B alone
statement: A can do a job in 10 days and B in 12 days. They work together for 3 days, after which A leaves. In how many days, in total, is the job finished?
explanation:

Total = 3 + 5.4 = **8.4 days**.

explanation:

A alone: 48 / 3 = **16 days**.

title: Sharing ₹9,100 between 18-day and 8-day workers
statement: A can do a job in 18 days and B in 8 days. They do it together and are paid ₹9,100 in all. What is A's fair share?
explanation:
Wages are shared in the ratio of work done, i.e. of daily rates 1/18 : 1/8 = 8 : 18.
A's share = 9100 × 8/26 = **₹2,800**. (Sharing in the ratio 18 : 8 rewards the slower worker.)

title: 15 men × 8 h/day lay 1 km in 10 days; 20 men × 10 h/day lay 1 km
statement: 15 men working 8 hours a day can lay a road 1 km long in 10 days. How many days will 20 men working 10 hours a day take to lay a road 1 km long?
explanation:
Work is proportional to men × days × hours: 15 × 10 × 8 man-hours lay 1 km.
1 km needs 1200 man-hours; per day the new team gives 20 × 10 = 200. Days = 1200/200 = **6 days**.

title: Working on alternate days: 4 days and 15 days
statement: A can finish a job in 4 days and B in 15 days. They work on alternate days, with A working on the first day. In how many days will the job be finished?
explanation:
Two days (A then B) complete 1/4 + 1/15 = 19/60 of the job. Count whole pairs of days, then finish the remainder with whoever works next.
Simulating day by day, the work is completed after **6.2 days**.
